title: Development of the human pancreas and its exocrine function.
authors: Mehta, Vijay; Hopson, Puanani E; Smadi, Yamen; Patel, Samit B; Horvath, Karoly; Mehta, Devendra I
one_liner_zh: 综述人胰腺发育及外分泌功能，涉及转录因子和基因调控，但无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: The pancreas has both endocrine and exocrine function and plays an important role in digestion and glucose control. Understanding the development of the pancreas, grossly and microscopically, and the genetic factors regulating it provides further insight into clinical problems that arise when these processes fail. Animal models of development are known to have inherent issues when understanding human development. Therefore, in this review, we focus on human studies that have reported gross and microscopic development including acinar-, ductal-, and endocrine cells and the neural network. We review the genes and transcription factors involved in organ formation using data from animal models to bridge current understanding where necessary. We describe the development of exocrine function in the fetus and postnatally. A deeper review of the genes involved in pancreatic formation allows us to describe the development of the different groups (proteases, lipids, and amylase) of enzymes during fetal life and postnatally and describe the genetic defects. We discuss the constellation of gross anatomical, as well as microscopic defects that with genetic mutations lead to pancreatic insufficiency and disease states.
abstract_zh: 胰腺兼具内分泌与外分泌功能，在消化和血糖调控中发挥重要作用。理解胰腺在肉眼及显微镜下的发育过程及其调控的遗传因素，有助于深入认识当这些过程异常时所引发的临床问题。已知动物发育模型在理解人类发育方面存在固有局限。因此，本综述聚焦于已报道的人类研究，涵盖肉眼及显微镜下发育，包括腺泡细胞、导管细胞、内分泌细胞及神经网络。我们利用动物模型数据，回顾参与器官形成的基因和转录因子，以在必要时桥接当前理解。我们描述了胎儿期及出生后外分泌功能的发育。通过深入探讨参与胰腺形成的基因，我们得以描述胎儿期及出生后不同酶类（蛋白酶、脂质酶和淀粉酶）的发育过程，并阐述相关遗传缺陷。我们讨论了在基因突变导致胰腺功能不全及疾病状态时，肉眼解剖及显微镜下缺陷的综合表现。
